subject: Performance & routing follow-up — latency, concurrency, and data residency (CoreWave)
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@corewavehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: Performance targets & multi-region routing (CoreWave)

Jonas / team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We walked through the integration surface and a few of the Redwood features we care about (prefix caching, canary rollouts, streaming support). A few follow-ups for our engineering team so we can scope the POC:

- Our rough latency targets: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms for short chat requests (payloads <= 1KB). For streaming (real-time transcription) we’re hoping for end-to-end p99 < 500ms in the US region.
- Expected steady-state throughput: 120 QPS overall, with spikes up to 600 QPS during business hours.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency per session ~ 6, but we have bursts where hundreds of concurrent sessions can be active.
- Traffic split by geography: US ~60%, EU ~30%, APAC ~10%.
- Data residency: EU at-rest data must stay in EU; APAC preference is Singapore; US in us-east.

Can you send a short post-call recap with the items you need from us to qualify perf/SLOs and a suggested routing strategy? Also please flag anything that would require Dedicated/Private (we’re evaluating compliance needs).

Best,
Emma Li
Head of Integrations, CoreWave Health
emma.li@corewavehealth.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@corewavehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets & multi-region routing (CoreWave)

Emma — thanks for the clear summary. Quick recap and concrete next steps from our side. I’m attaching a brief SLA matrix and a connection checklist to accelerate the POC.

Recap of what we heard (please correct if I mis-stated anything):
- Latency targets: p95 150ms (chat), streaming p99 500ms (US).
- Throughput: steady 120 QPS, burst to 600 QPS.
- Concurrency: per-session ~6, simultaneous active sessions can reach hundreds.
- Geo split: US 60 / EU 30 / APAC 10.
- Data residency constraints for EU and APAC.

What we need from you to size and propose the initial topology:
1) Representative payload sizes (average and 95th percentile) for chat and streaming chunks.
2) Typical session duration and average tokens per session (or average transcript length for streaming).
3) Expected read/write pattern to user data: are you sending hashes only, or full context to the model? Any retention windows?
4) Any hard SLA dates or compliance deadlines (Procurement timeline / SOC 2 evidence needed).

Suggested routing approach (first-pass):
- Default routing by geo-affinity: US requests -> us-east cluster; EU requests -> eu-west cluster with at-rest storage pinned to EU; APAC -> singapore edge cluster.
- Traffic steering: 90% primary routing, 10% spillover to a cost-optimized variant if latency is still within thresholds.
- Canary for streaming: small percentage (5–10%) routed to canary with lower-latency kernel and KV-cache warmers; promote once p99 meets target.

Notes about Dedicated vs Hosted: if EU data-at-rest in EU is non-negotiable and you require customer-managed KMS/HSM, Private deployment is recommended. Hosted can support EU residency at-rest with region pinning, but not with customer-managed HSM today.

Next steps:
- Emma: share the payload/token stats and retention policy (items 1–3 above).
- We (Redwood): run a quick topology proposal and rough cost/throughput estimates once we have numbers (target 48h).
- Set up a follow-up call this week to review proposed routing and canary plan.

Thanks — attaching postcall_sla_matrix.csv and redwood_connection_checklist.pdf for your team.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Adding ops notes and a suggested canary playbook.

Jonas — good summary. A couple of operational clarifications from CS/ops perspective:
- For streaming p99 500ms, we’ll want to validate the whole path (client -> edge -> model -> client). Please confirm codec + chunk size (e.g., 160ms audio frames vs 300ms). Smaller chunks help latency but increase QPS.
- KV cache behavior: are you expecting long-lived conversational state pinned to sessions? That will change memory footprint and kernel selection.
- Warm-up traffic pattern: we recommend a 24–72h warm window for KV caches with synthetic traffic before high-volume canary.

Suggested canary sequence (high level):
1) Smoke test (0.5% traffic) — basic correctness and connectivity checks.
2) Latency validation (5% traffic) — measure p50/p95/p99 against your targets.
3) Load ramp (5–20%) — step up to 20% with 15–30m holds, validate resource utilization.
4) Promote if metrics pass for 2 consecutive hours or revert on degradation.

I’ve attached a short playbook to demonstrate the checks and dashboards we’ll instrument. If CoreWave can provide a short synthetic generator that mimics your session concurrency distribution (6/session with bursts), we’ll run an internal pre-canary run in us-east and eu-west.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

---
Attachments: canary_playbook.md

From: Emma Li <emma.li@corewavehealth.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, platform@corewavehealth.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets & multi-region routing (CoreWave)

Thanks — answers below and I attached our security Q&A. Apologies for the fast replies.

Answers to your sizing questions:
- Payload sizes: chat average ~800 bytes; 95th percentile ~2.8KB. Streaming chunk sizes are ~320–480 bytes (we send ~200ms worth of audio per chunk, about ~256 bytes after encoding).
- Tokens/session: average 350 tokens per session; 95th percentile ~1,800 tokens. Typical session duration 3–7 minutes for chat, streaming sessions can be 30–90 minutes for live monitoring.
- Read/write pattern: we send the last 3 turns of context (plain text) plus a user id hash. We retain transcripts for 30 days for product analytics; EU transcripts must reside in EU for at-rest retention.
- Compliance timeline: procurement and legal are aiming to finalize T&Cs by end of August; SOC 2 evidence requested in the next 2–3 weeks.

Geo routing preference: we’d prefer geo-affinity (route by source IP) with the ability to override per-account for residency. For APAC, Singapore would be ideal — if Singapore cluster is expensive we can consider routing APAC to us-west as a fallback for non-sensitive workloads.

Streaming requirement clarification: the 500ms p99 target is strict for US production. For EU and APAC we can tolerate higher p99 (EU 700–900ms, APAC 900–1200ms) initially.

Attachments: CoreWave_Security_Answers_v2.docx

Next steps: I’ll get a synthetic generator for your warm-up run and share our procurement timeline with procurement@corewavehealth.com. Let us know if you need a short call to walk through the security doc.

Emma
